Designing participatory formats to promote understanding of soil health

At the Competence Center for Education and Social Transformation (CEST) at the University of St. Gallen, I design and implement participatory blended-learning formats for international target groups as part of the EU projectNEMESIS SOIL. The focus lies on creating interactive learning environments in which participants independently work on real-world challenges and collaboratively develop solutions. In this context, I design and deliver webinars, workshops, and digital exchange formats, coordinate their implementation across six European pilot sites, and manage collaboration with relevant stakeholders.

Designing hands-on STEM experiences that turn complexity into curiosity

At Hoffmann-La Roche’s Schoollab Experio, I work on designing and implementing hands-on STEM workshops that bring scientific concepts to life for students. My role involves not only running sessions in the lab, but also helping to develop new teaching formats and digital learning experiences. I adapt our offerings to meet the different needs of each class - some benefit from structured guidance, while others thrive with more autonomy and space to explore. This experience has deepened my understanding of how learning environments can be both creative and functional, and how didactic clarity and flexibility can go hand in hand. It has also sharpened my skills in translating complex content into engaging, age-appropriate learning formats - both analogue and digital.

Exploring learner needs - deepening educational research experience

As a student assistant in the Learning to Adapt, Learning with Agency Lab led by Professor Tomohiro Nagashima within the Technology-Enhanced Learning research group at Saarland University, I contributed to a qualitative research project examining how students, teachers, and other stakeholders perceive and prefer the use of AI tools in educational settings. My work focused on the design and conduct of semi-structured interviews with teachers, as well as the analysis and interpretation of qualitative data. I also used storyboards to develop realistic user scenarios, which informed both the interview design and the analytical process. Through this experience, I further developed my skills in user-centered research, particularly in identifying educational needs, comparing stakeholder perspectives, and translating insights into design-relevant implications for digital learning systems.

First experiences in industrial work environments

During my time as a working student at ZF Friedrichshafen, I was involved in production line work, assembling automotive transmissions as part of a large-scale manufacturing process. This hands-on experience gave me valuable insight into the dynamics, routines, and demands of industrial environments. It shaped my understanding of what it means to work in structured, process-driven settings – and deepened my awareness of how learning and communication need to be tailored to meet the needs of people in such contexts.
